subject: Art & Design
title: Personal Branding: You Are a Brand
description: A micro-lesson that makes Personal Branding: You Are a Brand usable.

hook.text: Google your name. Whatever appears IS your personal brand.

buildup.text: Personal branding applies business principles to individuals: positioning, visual consistency, voice, and audience.

discovery.text: LinkedIn profiles, portfolios, social media aesthetics, and email signatures all form your visual brand system.

twist.text: Personal Branding has a twist: the obvious interpretation usually breaks down.

climax.text: Designers like Aaron Draplin and Jessica Walsh built empires by being unmistakably themselves. Voice + visuals + values.

punchline.text: You don't need to be famous. You need to be recognizable to the right people.

quiz.question: What is the foundation of a strong personal brand?
options: An authentic, recognizable point of view expressed consistently
Having the most followers on social media
A professionally designed logo and business card

details.summary: Personal branding applies corporate identity principles to individuals — defining a professional reputation through consistent messaging, visual presentation, and online presence.
details.whyItMatters: In a competitive job market, everyone has a brand whether they manage it or not. Deliberate personal branding ensures that the impression you make matches the career you want, rather than leaving your reputation to chance.
takeaways: Applies corporate branding principles to individual reputation
LinkedIn, portfolios, and social media shape professional perception
Deliberate branding matches your impression to your career goals

faq.question: How do you build a personal brand?
faq.answer: Define what you want to be known for — your unique value proposition. Ensure your LinkedIn, portfolio, social media, and professional interactions consistently communicate that message. Share expertise through content, speaking, or writing.

faq.question: Is personal branding just self-promotion?
faq.answer: Not when done well. Effective personal branding focuses on providing value to others — sharing knowledge, helping connections, and demonstrating expertise through action. Self-promotional personal brands feel hollow. The strongest personal brands are built by consistently delivering value.
